title: FDP-Det: An Infrared Object Detection Network Integrating Frequency–Spatial Detail Enhancement and Text Prototypes
content: Infrared object detection exploits thermal-radiation differences between objects and backgrounds to support pedestrian and vehicle localization and recognition under low illumination for nighttime road monitoring. However, limited texture, low contrast, and complex backgrounds constrain structural representation, cross-scale detail transfer, and similar-class discrimination in lightweight detectors. A Frequency–Detail–Prototype Detector (FDP-Det) is proposed based on YOLO11n from the You Only Look Once (YOLO) family, integrating frequency–spatial detail enhancement and text prototypes. To separately enhance coarse structures and high-frequency directional details, Hierarchical Frequency–Spatial Encoding (HFSE) combines two-level wavelet subband processing with parallel spatial convolution. To provide local structural guidance for nearest-neighbor upsampling, Detail-Guided Transfer (DGT) jointly predicts neighborhood reassembly weights from coarse and shallow features for bounded residual correction. To supplement visual-only discrimination under limited texture, Prototype-Coupled Discrimination (PCD) projects offline class text prototypes and visual features into a shared space, adding similarity scores residually to visual classification logits. The modules share a detection pathway and are jointly optimized through detection loss. Mean average precision (mAP) improves from 46.7% to 48.3% at mAP@50 and from 27.5% to 28.7% at mAP@50:95 compared with YOLO11n. Cross-scenario generalization experiments further confirm effectiveness and robustness.
